story: Manco Cápac, also called Ayar Manco, was said to have emerged from a cave at Tamputoco (Paqariq Tampu) with his three brothers, Ayar Auca, Ayar Cachi, and Ayar Uchu, and four sisters, including Mama Ocllo, carrying a golden staff given to him by his father, the creator god Viracocha. Traveling together, the siblings joined with other peoples they met and sought to conquer the tribes of the Cusco Valley. Manco Cápac caused his three brothers to be trapped or turned to stone, leaving him sole leader. He then married his elder sister, Mama Ocllo, and together they defeated three small tribes—the Sahuares, Huallas, and Alcahuisas—and settled in a marshy area between two streams, founding the city of Cusco, later divided into four districts. Though small, the city was surrounded by larger tribes, such as the confederated Ayarmacas and Pinaguas, who often attacked it, forcing Manco Cápac and later his son Sinchi Roca to defend it. After his natural death, his son succeeded him, and his mummified body remained in Cusco until Pachacuti ordered it moved to the Temple of the Sun on Isla del Sol, leaving only a statue in the city. In another version, Manco Cápac was the son of the sun god Inti and the moon goddess Mama Killa, sent to earth with his siblings to build a temple where the golden staff, called tapac-yauri, sank into the ground; they traveled through caves to Cusco and built the temple there. A further account holds that Manco Cápac was the son of the sorceress Mama Waqu, who tricked the people of Cusco into making her queen, secretly bore and hid her son, then revealed him as a divine child destined to rule; she married him, and they reigned together.
